headline_marked: Post-Commit Hook Demanded Rewrite of [[8 Pushed Commits]]; Developer Refused
headline: Post-Commit Hook Demanded Rewrite of 8 Pushed Commits; Developer Refused
summary: A post-commit hook flagged 8 commits as 'Unverified' and suggested rewriting them. The developer refused, citing potential history corruption and policy violations.
details: A developer encountered a post-commit hook that flagged 8 pushed commits as 'Unverified' and offered to rewrite them by setting the committer identity. This hook's proposed fix was problematic because it would have overwritten existing, correct committer information and potentially rewritten shared history.

Upon inspection, six of the eight commits already had a valid committer (noreply@anthropic.com), indicating the issue was a missing GPG/SSH signature, not a missing identity. Only one commit had a local email address as the committer. The hook's diagnosis did not match the actual problem for most commits.

The hook's suggested fix involved rewriting already pushed commits, which requires a force-push and can corrupt shared history if not handled carefully. The agent executing the hook did not have authorization for such actions on the main branch.

Furthermore, the hook's suggestion to set the committer identity to 'Claude' violated the repository's policy against AI attribution in commit metadata. This policy is enforced through a deterministic strip filter to prevent AI credit in commit messages and now, apparently, in committer identities.

The developer chose not to execute the hook's fix, leaving the 'Unverified' badges as they were and documenting the issue. The actual solution for unverified commits is typically to set up commit signing with a GPG or SSH key, a low-risk change.

The key takeaway is that unattended agents should not blindly execute hooks that rewrite pushed history or alter identity fields. A clear policy should define which hook outputs are auto-applied and which require manual review to prevent accidental data corruption or policy violations.

headline_marked: iOS 27 beta 4 [[adds Automatic Downloads]] for Apple TV app
headline: iOS 27 beta 4 adds Automatic Downloads for Apple TV app
summary: Apple's latest beta for iOS 27 introduces a new feature for the Apple TV app, allowing for automatic downloads of content.
details: Apple has released the fourth beta version of iOS 27, bringing a new functionality to the Apple TV application. This update focuses on improving the user experience by enabling automatic downloads.

The new 'Automatic Downloads' feature in the Apple TV app allows users to have content downloaded automatically. This means that new episodes of shows or other content they are following will be downloaded in the background without manual intervention.

This feature is particularly useful for users who want to ensure they always have the latest content available for offline viewing, especially when they have a stable Wi-Fi connection. It streamlines the process of keeping up with favorite shows and movies.

The release of iOS 27 beta 4 also hints at other potential features and improvements, including a major AI upgrade for Siri, as previously reported. Apple is continuously refining its operating systems with beta releases to test new functionalities before the official public launch.
